name: maybe_Ui_JackpotScreen_CtorParts
summary: Second-stage setup/teardown of the casino jackpot screen: for the current screen index it releases the reel object, the slot-symbol object and the animation object, then re-registers them. Register artifacts (unaff_r5/r6/r8, in_d8) keep the exact staging unproven.
evidence: No callers at all and all four callees are casino-UI objects (Ui_RouletteWindow_BuildReels, Ui_SlotSymbol_DeletingDtor, Ui_Object_PlayAnimationPoor_DtorDelete, 0x002C8EA2); the casino attribution is solid but the 'CtorParts' stage wording is not.

name: maybe_Camera_UpdateScreenTargets
signature: void maybe_Camera_UpdateScreenTargets(CameraWork* cameraWork, float* out, u32 flags, u32* extra)
summary: Per-screen camera target pass: advances the target timer, releases the previous target handle when the timer expires, builds a setup record, applies Camera_SetupFromRecord and rebuilds the visible target lists. Called once per frame by Camera_UpdateScreenViews.
evidence: Corrected the action: the body is a timer-driven target-handle swap (Camera_ReleaseTargetHandle -> Camera_SetupFromRecord -> Camera_BuildVisibleTargetLists -> Camera_UpdateWorkEntry), not a 'follow position' blend; its only caller is Camera_UpdateScreenViews. Damaged registers still block a confident name.

name: maybe_Camera_UpdateFollowPositionEx
signature: void maybe_Camera_UpdateFollowPositionEx(float dt, u32 flags, float arg3, float* out)
summary: Not an independent function: this is the decompiler's mid-function split tail of 0x001D1FC4 (same camera target pass, overlapping instruction at 0x001D222C). It exists only because the caller was split, so the name must stay a maybe_ placeholder.
evidence: Only caller is 0x001D1FC4 itself and the body starts mid-sequence (register0x54-relative spills, unaff_r4/r6..r11); no new evidence supports an 'Ex' variant.

name: maybe_Battle_Ui_UpdateStateMachine
summary: Battle-UI sequence step: bails out when the battle work is not in 3D mode, flushes pending battle log entries, then runs a state machine that walks a row array and polls each row object's vtable (+0x10/+0x18/+0x1C) until all rows report done.
evidence: Only readable body available (recovered file, no dossier): it reads battle work +0x4244 and calls Battle_Ui_FlushPendingLogEntries, so the Battle_Ui prefix holds, but the body is damaged (0 bytes recovered, bad instruction data at 0x00389286) and no caller confirms the state-machine role.

name: maybe_Battle_Ui_ActorFocusSequence_Update
summary: Battle-UI sequence that focuses the view on one or two actors: state 0x7DC updates the target markers, then it reads the actor field transform, lays out balloons and member anchors and computes the group midpoint. Bad instruction data truncates the tail.
evidence: Corrected the subsystem: every named callee is battle UI (Ui_BattleTargetMarker_UpdatePositions, Battle_Ui_LayoutBalloons, Battle_Ui_GetMemberAnchor, Battle_OrientActorAndGetGroupMidpoint) and the only caller is 0x004BFF56 in the battle UI sequence, so 'Field_' was wrong; the sequence role itself is still only described.

name: maybe_Party_GetMessageTokenParams
summary: Large (9 KB) routine that walks the living party, matches skills/states and equipment, and fills a small token result; named callers are the message-argument builders Ui_Window_BuildMessageArgFromToken and Ui_Window_GetMessageArg, plus 0x0063AD40.
evidence: The named callers pin the message-argument consumer side, but the body is heavily damaged (in_d8, many unaff) and one caller (Anim_Clip_IsFinished) is clearly misnamed, so what the token actually contains is still unclear.

name: Field_Npc_InitColorBalloonA
signature: void Field_Npc_InitColorBalloonA(FieldNpc* self, const NpcPlacement* placement, const u32* color, u32 owner)
summary: NPC spawn initialiser (variant A): copies the placement transform and bounds, stores the colour word and talk/animation ids, sets the balloon flags, then builds the talk-balloon sprite child plus the model. Its default talk action comes from g_npcColorBalloonADefaultTalkAction.
evidence: Confirmed: the named global g_npcColorBalloonADefaultTalkAction is used verbatim and the body is a complete placement-record initialiser (Field_Actor_CreateSprite, Model_SetupObject, Field_CreateActorResourceSet, Gfx_SpriteActor_AddChildC). Only the caller 0x00341394 is still unnamed.

name: Field_Npc_InitColorBalloonB
signature: void Field_Npc_InitColorBalloonB(FieldNpc* self, const NpcPlacement* placement, const u32* color, u32 owner)
summary: NPC spawn initialiser (variant B): same placement-transform/colour/balloon setup as variant A but reading the second record layout (+0x19, +0x5A..+0x5D) and using g_npcColorBalloonBDefaultTalkAction.
evidence: Confirmed by the distinct named global g_npcColorBalloonBDefaultTalkAction and the same initialiser callee set; the two variants differ only in the placement record offsets.

name: Field_Actor_UpdatePoseAnim
summary: Per-frame field-actor animation update: resolves the party member record from self+0x8B, checks whether the actor may be a camera target, picks a pose/weapon animation id and blends the body transform toward it (Math_Vec3Slerp, std_FastSinCos).
evidence: Confirmed by its two named callers Field_Actor_ApplyWeaponAnim and Field_Npc_UpdateModelFromTable plus the named callee Field_Actor_SetWeaponAnimTime: the function drives the actor's weapon/pose animation clock. The body is damaged (unaff_r10) only in the tail.

name: maybe_Fx_UpdateParticleG
summary: Integrates one particle of emitter type G through the shared per-particle pipeline (offset, target, keyframe scale, position) and appends its node data; called once per particle from the particle-list dispatchers.
evidence: Called once per particle by the named list updaters Fx_UpdateParticleListL/N/Q and it calls Fx_AppendNodeData, so it belongs to the confident Fx_UpdateParticle family, but the body is damaged (bad instruction data plus dozens of unreachable-block removals), so the letter stays a maybe_ placeholder.

name: maybe_Gfx_ModelInstance_DrawShadowPass
signature: void maybe_Gfx_ModelInstance_DrawShadowPass(Gfx_ModelInstance* self, int cmdList, unsigned arg3, int* state, int* mode)
summary: Model-instance render pass selected by the material flag f_254: builds a projection from the screen dimensions and material offsets f_BC/f_C0, stamps the command block and emits every part through BindTextureAndDraw.
evidence: Called only from Gfx_ModelInstance_DrawPassDispatcher when f_254==1, but the matrices are screen-space projections built from 0x1E0/400/0x140 render sizes, not light matrices, so 'shadow' remains a guess; kept maybe_.

name: maybe_Battle_Ui_RowPanel_UpdateB
summary: Battle party-status window step: runs a 0x559-entry state machine over the member rows, advances the row/column counters, and calls the anchor/transform and dual-hand-weapon helpers to animate the panel.
evidence: Callees (Battle_Ui_GetMemberAnchor, Battle_Ui_RowPanel_ApplyTransform, Party_Member_HasDualHandWeapon) and the panel state field win+0xC98 fit the name, but the only caller 0x0059DC9A is unnamed and the body has bad instruction data, so the B variant stays unproven.

name: maybe_Field_ComputeActorPlacementPoint
signature: void maybe_Field_ComputeActorPlacementPoint(float* out, void* arg2, void* record, void* camera, void* arg5)
summary: Computes a camera-relative world placement point for a field actor: derives an offset from the camera quaternion, the character record height and the actor bytes +0x32/+0x33, jitters it with the field RNG and clamps it with Camera_FindEntryCoveringPosition/Camera_IsTargetWithinRange.
evidence: Corrected: both named callers (Field_NpcGetActionAnimId, Field_NpcJumpAction_PlanPath) consume a world point and the routine never projects to screen space, so 'ActorScreenPosition' was misleading; the field-NPC placement use is what the call sites prove.

name: maybe_Field_Object2D_UpdateCameraRelativeSprite
summary: Advances a camera-facing sprite along its distance curve (f_2F4/f_2F8/f_300/f_310 of the effect part), rebuilds the billboard basis, draws the sprite variant and releases the effect when the curve is exhausted.
evidence: No callers; the curve/fade fields and Gfx_Scene_SpriteCtx_Init/Math_Curve_GetPosition callees match the description, but the owning class (Field_Object2D) is inferred from layout only.

name: Gfx_UpdateTrailTransform
summary: Per-frame trail/ribbon transform update: resets the node scale, composes the object's stored 4x3 matrix with the identity basis, derives the trail orientation from the target direction and writes the resulting node scale.
evidence: Confirmed by its two named callers Model_Attach_ResetTransform / Model_Attach_ResetTransformB and the trail-specific fields it owns (f_5DC scale, f_599 parent flag, sample index f_6DC, matrices at f_624/f_6CC).

name: Battle_CalcMemberStatScale
summary: Returns a member stat as a percentage scale: resolves the party member record, reads the per-stat float tables at +0x998/+0xD58 (special case index 7 summing +0xB68/+0xF28/+0xD74/+0x1134), multiplies by 0.01f and folds in the status-0x4F variance roll.
evidence: Confirmed: all three callers are battle maths/UI rows (Battle_RollMultiHitDamage, Battle_Message_BuildConditionRow, 0x0048FA08) and the body uses the documented PartyMember float tables plus Battle_CalcRandomDamageVariance.

name: Battle_Ui_MemberScreen_UpdateMemberPose
summary: Sub-update of the battle member screen: resolves the battle unit's actor entry through Field_FindActorEntryByModel, copies its transform blocks and applies the layout/anim helper calls that position the member portrait model.
evidence: Confirmed by its single named caller Battle_Ui_MemberScreen_UpdateB (same screen class) and the actor-entry/anchor callee set; only the per-slot pose wording is descriptive.

name: maybe_Field_Gimmick_ArrangeMembersCircle
signature: void maybe_Field_Gimmick_ArrangeMembersCircle(FieldGimmick* gimmick, int arg2, int arg3)
summary: Places the members of an actor group on a circle: fills an 0x10-byte place record, derives the angular spacing with std_FastSinCos/std_Acosf, names the motion from the 'Bt_Nut' base string and places each member with Field_ActorGroup_PlaceMember.
evidence: No callers (vtable only); Field_ActorGroup_PlaceMember plus the 'Bt_Nut' string literal support the arrangement role, but the gimmick class and 'circle' wording are inferred from the trig loop.

name: maybe_Menu_UpdateModelFadeIn
summary: Gates the battle intro model fade-in: waits for all four unit lists (state+0x4254 / +0x428C) to report ready, advances the fade step counter up to 3 and averages the per-actor fade values measured by Menu_MeasureActorHeight/Menu_MeasureAverageActorWidth.
evidence: Both callers are named battle update code (Battle_Update, Battle_UpdateUnitDisplay), which makes the 'Menu_' prefix doubtful, but the fade-in gate is clear from the +0x4D74 step counter; kept maybe_ because the owning class is a battle work, not a menu.

name: maybe_Field_DragonJumpAction_Update
summary: Update of the dragon-jump field action: samples the scene box set at the actor position, reads the combined move vector, normalises it and rotates the actor along the jump arc with Math_QuatFromAxisAngle.
evidence: No callers; the jump reading rests on the 'Dragon_Jump' data block that follows the function and on the arc maths, not on a named caller.

name: Field_FindFreePlacementPoint3D
summary: Searches for a collision-free 3D placement point: starts from the current camera/player transform, sweeps the eight offsets of g_fieldPlacementSearchOffsets3D with sin/cos, and rejects hits with the field collision raycast and rect tests.
evidence: Confirmed by the named search table g_fieldPlacementSearchOffsets3D (copied verbatim into the local offset array) and Field_Collision_RaycastScene/Field_Scene_RectIntersectsSetA; still no caller, so only the 3D-vs-2D wording is inferred.

name: maybe_Field_ActorAction_UpdateMoveDirection
summary: Writes the actor's move direction for the frame: in scripted mode takes Field_GetCombinedMoveVector, otherwise Input_ReadMoveStick3D / Input_ReadLookStick3D, normalises the result and rotates it by the actor quaternion into the output vector.
evidence: No callers and the 'ActorAction' owner is just the parameter type; the direction maths is clear (Field_GetCombinedMoveVector, Field_Actor_GetRotationQuat, stick readers) and this is exactly what the old name says, so it stays a maybe_.

name: maybe_Battle_Ui_RowPanel_UpdateMemberB
summary: Per-member step of the party status panel: resolves the model record, advances the bar progress (1/columnSpan + accumulator), copies the actor entry and asks Battle_Ui_GetMemberAnchorScreen / Battle_GetUnitModelSizeIf3D for the bar anchor.
evidence: The bar/anchor callees fit, but this variant's only caller is the equally unnamed 0x0059D638, so the B-variant attribution is unproven.

name: maybe_BattleScene_InitAnimSlots
summary: Battle-scene initialisation: starts four Anim_TimeTrack slots at scene+0x308, then walks the four 0x1C-stride battle unit lists (+0x428C) and sets the effect-part orientation/scale for units whose model id is 0x18F or 0x1A5.
evidence: Corrected the subsystem: the only caller is BattleScene_UpdateState and the body reads battle work (work+8)->f_5C unit lists, so 'Gfx_SceneSprite2D' / 'FieldLevel' was wrong; the anim-slot part is exactly the four Anim_TimeTrack_Init calls.

name: maybe_Effect_MeshEmitter_SetupB
summary: Mesh-emitter setup variant B: stores def fields, builds the fixed string 'Open' (0x6E65704F), applies the transform/rotation, adds the sprite child and colour animator, and creates the mesh object.
evidence: Only caller is the unnamed spawn block 0x0034D08B region (maybe_Field_SceneSpawnBlock_EffectMeshEmitterB); the 'Open' literal and the mesh/child sequence match its sibling variant C, so the family is clear but the emitter class is inferred.

name: maybe_Effect_MeshEmitter_SetupC
summary: Mesh-emitter setup variant C: same sprite child, colour animator and mesh creation as 0x0040FBB8 but stores the fixed string 'Off' (0x0066664F) and sets the active state byte to 1.
evidence: Only caller is the unnamed spawn block for effect mesh emitter C; 'Off' versus 'Open' is the whole difference to its sibling, so the variant letter is reliable but the owning class is not.

name: maybe_Battle_Monster_GetAttackPowerB
summary: Monster UI stat B: resolves the party member record, scales the display-slot factor by 0.01, and returns (f_EB8 + f_738*scale + f_AF8) * variantScale where variantScale is 0.5 or 1.0 from member byte +0x665.
evidence: Same three-field formula as 0x00496B50 and 0x0048FCA4 and the callers are rows of Battle_MonsterUI_Dispatch / Battle_Monster_CalcBarSpan, so it is a displayed monster-UI stat; nothing in the body proves the field is attack power, so maybe_ stays.

name: Fx_UpdateParticleD
summary: Integrates one particle of emitter type D: advances position by velocity, applies the two fade tables (f_294/f_295), updates scale from the keyframe table and moves the particle toward its target.
evidence: Confirmed as part of the family whose E member (0x005257E8 Fx_UpdateParticleE) already carries a confident name: two named list updaters (Fx_UpdateParticleListQ/T) call it per particle and the callees are the shared Fx_UpdateParticle* pipeline.

name: Fx_UpdateParticleH
summary: Integrates one particle of emitter type H: stamps the emitter command block, copies the keyframe velocities, applies the gravity/fade factors and advances position, target and scale.
evidence: Confirmed by its three list-updater callers (Fx_UpdateParticleListL/Q and 0x0052D010) and the shared callee set (Fx_AddParticleOffset, Fx_UpdateParticleTarget, Fx_AdvanceEmitterFrame); same family as the confident Fx_UpdateParticleE.

name: maybe_FieldNpc_DrawPartyIcon
summary: Draws the floating icon above a field NPC: lazily creates the shared 0x98-byte icon object, resolves the icon record from the id at self+0x258, looks up the party entry by self+0x38C and draws the icon at the NPC position with the state-byte colour scaling.
evidence: No callers. Party_FindEntryById and the story-table lookup support the party-icon reading, but the actual draw call is through 0x006282D0/unnamed helpers, so the icon semantics stay inferred.

name: maybe_Field_Gimmick_UpdateVariantLayout
signature: void maybe_Field_Gimmick_UpdateVariantLayout(FieldGimmick* self, int arg2, int variant)
summary: Variant-driven gimmick step: switches on variant 0..7 to choose the effect count, action id and SE id, moves the gimmick parts and plays the sound through Sound_PlaySeById.
evidence: No named callers; the variant switch and Sound_PlaySeById/Gfx_EffectPart_SetDirection callees match the description, but the gimmick class and 'layout' wording are inferred.

name: maybe_Ui_Toggle_Init
summary: Initialises a small two-state icon object for the casino jackpot screen: zeroes the 0x18 header, loads the syscmn.bch node names 'g3085'/'g3085_jp' and creates the sprite through the jackpot screen helper.
evidence: Only caller is Ui_JackpotScreen_Ctor and the node literals come from syscmn.bch, so the jackpot-screen ownership is solid; 'toggle' is an interpretation of the two node names.

name: maybe_Gfx_SpriteActor_InitFromDescSmall
summary: Descriptor-driven billboard initialiser: sets flag 0, copies desc position/param bytes, selects the sprite mode from desc byte 0x3E, builds the quad child for modes 3/4 and creates the mesh with the smaller scale/alpha constants.
evidence: No callers; the body is identical to 0x00471ABC except f_2C9 and three float constants, so 'Small'/'Large' records the measured constant set rather than a verified size class.

name: maybe_Gfx_SpriteActor_InitFromDescLarge
summary: Descriptor-driven billboard initialiser: identical to 0x004718A4 but sets flag f_2C9 = 1 and uses the larger scale/alpha constants for the quad child and mesh.
evidence: No callers; the only differences to the 'Small' twin are the flag byte and three float constants, so the size-class wording cannot be verified.

name: maybe_Ui_ModelView_UpdateModelRotation
summary: Builds an axis-angle quaternion from the view's orbit angle and applies it to the model when the global rebuild flag is clear and the camera child at (work+8)->f_74->f_40 exists.
evidence: No callers and no vtable reference; the rotation maths is clear but the owning class (UiModelView) is inferred from the field names only.

name: Model_SetTrailTarget
signature: void Model_SetTrailTarget(Model* model, const float* targetPos, const float* targetDir)
summary: Stores the trail anchor position on the model (f_27..f_29), normalises the target direction into the effect part, rebuilds the pattern transform and resets the trail samples through Gfx_Trail_ResetSamples.
evidence: Confirmed by Gfx_Trail_ResetSamples being called on the same object and by Model_UpdatePatternTransform; the caller Ui_Overlay_ApplySlotSetup only supplies the anchor, the trail part is in the callee set.

name: maybe_Actor_UpdateDirectionBlend
summary: Scripted movement integrator for action ids 0x253..0x25B: blends the stored direction toward the target with the g_playerActor3DDefaultParams easing (std_Powf), renormalises it and hands the transform to Gfx_Node_UpdateChildren.
evidence: No callers; the action-id range check and the easing/renormalise sequence support the description, but the owner is only the parameter type.

name: Gfx_Trail_BuildRibbon
signature: void Gfx_Trail_BuildRibbon(void* trail, const void* sample, const void* offset, u8 flags)
summary: Shifts the 0xEE-entry ribbon history (0x40 bytes per entry), computes a camera-facing perpendicular offset for the new sample and inserts the new control point.
evidence: Confirmed by its named caller Actor_UpdateFollowTarget and by Gfx_GetSceneSpriteContext being used to get the camera basis; the 0xEE-entry history shift is unmistakable ribbon building.

name: Gfx_Actor_ApplyMotion
summary: Commits the actor's stored motion to its scene object: mode 0/1 copy position and direction (0 also notifies the effect owner), mode 2 hands the offset target to Gfx_SpriteActor_MoveTowardPoint, mode 3 normalises and moves toward the rotated point.
evidence: Confirmed by the three named callers (MessageFunc, ActorSetShadow, Actor_ApplyMotionAndModelSize) and by the named Gfx_EffectPart_SetTargetPoint / Gfx_SpriteActor_MoveTowardPoint callees: this is the shared motion commit of the actor-motion module.

name: maybe_Battle_Unit_UpdateActionState
signature: u32 maybe_Battle_Unit_UpdateActionState(BattleUnitView* view, BattleUnit* unit, int* faceData, u32 flags)
summary: Per-frame update of a battle unit's model view: ticks the animation channels and motion state and, when the animation ends, resolves the unit's face/expression row and plays its recorded SE.
evidence: No callers; the anim/motion callees are named but 'action state' is a description of the animation state, not a proven engine concept.

name: maybe_Battle_Monster_GetAttackPower
summary: Monster UI stat (row kind 10): resolves the party member record, mixes f_73C, f_AF8 and f_EBC with the Battle_Enemy_GetDisplaySlot factor and marks the row layout dirty.
evidence: Only caller is Battle_MonsterUI_Dispatch for row kind 10; the field triple is shared with 0x004973E8 / 0x0048FCA4 and the row layout is dirtied, so it is a displayed stat value, but nothing identifies it as attack power.

name: maybe_Battle_Unit_UpdateSkullRunPose
summary: Battle copy of the 'Skull_Run' pose update: forces the model's Skull_Run animation node, derives the facing basis and acos angle from the node position and hands the aim to Math_Vec3_LookAtRotationMatrix.
evidence: Corrected the action: the function poses an actor (same body as 0x004F129C) and never touches an anchor, so 'UpdateSkullRunAnchor' described it wrongly; the battle-side ownership is inferred from the twin split, not from a caller.

name: maybe_Field_Gimmick_LayoutPartsFromAnchor
summary: Lays out the owner actor's child parts from an anchor basis: stores half the anchor distance in f_20, iterates the parts with 0x00650D34 placing them along the basis and plays the SE; also hides a UI panel through Ui_GetCore vt[+0x28].
evidence: No callers; Gfx_EffectPart_SetDirection/Field_SceneObject_ShowAndSelectEntry plus the part loop support the layout reading, but 'anchor' and the gimmick class are inferred.

name: Field_Scene_TestPointInBoxSet
summary: Tests a world point against the scene's oriented-box set: copies the 0x60-byte box record from scene+0x38C, converts the point into the box frame with Math_BuildQuaternionFromEuler/Math_BuildBoundsFromSphereAndOffset and returns on the first containing box.
evidence: Confirmed by its named caller Event_Rura_Start and by the sibling predicate Field_Scene_IsPointInsideBoxSetA; Ghidra only dropped the boolean return, which the hit early-outs make clear.

name: Ui_Layout_BuildQuadTransforms
signature: void Ui_Layout_BuildQuadTransforms(LayoutSet* layoutSet, u32 dstBuffer, u32 count, LayoutEntry* entries, float scale)
summary: Turns layout sprite records into per-quad vertex coordinates: handles the rotated path with std_FastSinCos and the arbitrary-quad UV path, caches the result behind a built flag and delegates the per-element maths to Ui_LayoutElement_BuildTransform.
evidence: Confirmed by twelve callers, ten of them named UI layout code (Ui_Part_SetupFromAnimRecord, Ui_Part_SetupAttachFromRecord, Ui_Widget_ApplyScreenTransform, Ui_Poker_SetCardSprite, Ui_SlotNumberPlate3D_Init) plus Gfx_Sprite_SetFrameUV, all of which need quad corners.

name: maybe_Ui_Part_UpdateSlotTransforms
signature: void maybe_Ui_Part_UpdateSlotTransforms(void* part, u32 frame, u32* timer)
summary: Per-frame transform update for an effect part: rebuilds up to four slot rotations from the angle fields with trig helpers, applies the stored transform blocks, clamps the part bounding box and sets the sound-emitter position/direction.
evidence: Only caller is Ui_HorseraceReceptMsg_Release (itself suspicious), and the callee set mixes sound-emitter and AABB helpers, so the owning class is unclear.

name: maybe_Ui_SpriteActor_CreateCharacterSprite
summary: Builds a 2D character sprite for a UI sprite actor: resolves the character data row, creates the sprite child and colour animator and attaches them to the actor.
evidence: Only caller is the unnamed 0x002B535C; Data_FindRowByPackedKeys and Gfx_SpriteActor_AddChildC support the sprite-creation reading but the character/UI attribution is inferred.

name: maybe_Field_Gimmick_MoveAttachmentTowardTarget
summary: Clears the attachment, computes and normalises the direction from the attachment to the target fields, applies the step scaled by f_234, updates the attachment and plays the SE.
evidence: No callers; Field_Actor_UpdateAttachment and the normalise/step sequence match, but the gimmick owner and the meaning of the f_234 step scale are unproven.

name: maybe_Trail_UpdateGeometry
summary: Rebuilds the trail/ribbon vertex geometry for the frame: samples the spline points, rebuilds the basis with Math_RebuildBasis and constructs the quad-strip vertices.
evidence: Callers are Gfx_Node_UpdateChildren and 0x003D98C0; the geometry rebuild is clear but the object is a generic child node, so 'Trail' is inferred.

name: Ui_Overlay_CalcAnchorMatrix
signature: void Ui_Overlay_CalcAnchorMatrix(u32* outMatrix, UiOverlay* overlay, u32 nodeId)
summary: Builds the world transform of a UI-overlay anchor node: seeds the output with identity, overwrites the basis with the node matrix, composes the model frame and skeleton scale and writes the resulting position.
evidence: Confirmed by all five named callers (Camera_ResolveCollision, Camera_Update, Battle_Ui_PlaceMarkerOnModel, Ui_Overlay_FindTargetUnderCursor, Model_ComputeAttachmentAnchor), which each resolve an anchor id with Ui_Overlay_GetAnchorIdByName first.

name: maybe_Menu_CheckActorAnimationDone
summary: Scans the four party lists for the actor resolved by Monster_LookupRecord, compares the record frame counter with a threshold and updates a per-actor retry counter before reporting done.
evidence: No callers. The scan/threshold part matches the old name, but the body also calls Math_RandomChanceBelow, which a pure 'animation done' predicate should not need, so the verdict is probably incomplete.

name: Field_ActorAction_UpdateJump
summary: Integrates a field actor jump: applies gravity and vertical velocity from g_fieldActorActionJumpParam/Gravity, queries the ground, clamps Y to the ground range via Field_WrapPositionXZ and snaps the actor on landing.
evidence: Confirmed by the named jump globals g_fieldActorActionJumpParam/Gravity and by Field_ActorAction_PlayStateAnim / Field_Actor_CanUpdate being the surrounding action helpers; no caller only because it is called through the action vtable.

name: Fx_UpdateParticleA
summary: Per-particle integration step for emitter type A: advances position by velocity, applies the steering offset, the keyframe scale and the target pull, then hands the particle to the oriented emitter.
evidence: Confirmed by the two list updaters that call it once per particle (0x0052D010, 0x0052DF78) and by the shared Fx_UpdateParticlePosition/Fx_AddParticleOffset/Fx_UpdateParticleTarget callees; the letter is only a family ordinal.

name: maybe_Gfx_Effect_UpdatePlacement
summary: Projects the effect's world offset to screen space, scales it by the camera distance clamped to the near/far range, and lets the owner apply the result through virtual slot +0x24.
evidence: No callers; Gfx_ProjectWorldToScreen and the (work+8)->f_74 camera child are named, but the owning class only comes from the object layout.

name: Camera_ComputeViewTransform
signature: void Camera_ComputeViewTransform(float* out, CameraParams* params, float* src, float* target)
summary: Builds the camera view/orbit transform: normalises the look direction, derives yaw/pitch with std_Acosf, rotates the offset by the quaternion and writes eye position plus orientation components.
evidence: Confirmed by its only caller Camera_Field_Update and the pure camera maths (no game-work access at all); the exact output layout stays described rather than typed.

name: maybe_Monster_GetAttackStat
summary: Computes the f_738 + f_EB8 + f_AF8 monster stat triple, either raw or scaled by the Battle_Enemy_GetDisplaySlot factor, and marks the row layout dirty.
evidence: Same triple as 0x00496B50 / 0x004973E8, so it is the same displayed monster-UI stat, but its only caller is Field_CheckZonePoint (unrelated on its face) and nothing proves 'attack'.

name: maybe_Motion_ApplyRotationBlend
signature: void maybe_Motion_ApplyRotationBlend(float* out, Motion* first, Motion* second)
summary: Second half of the motion blend: rotates the blended offset with Math_QuatFromAxisAngle, normalises it and stores the resulting float3.
evidence: Only caller is Ui_MotionPath_UpdateTransform; the body is damaged (in_fpscr, float arguments arrive in s0), so the rotate/normalise reading is the most that can be said.

name: Actor_UpdateSkullRunPose
summary: Forces the model's 'Skull_Run' animation node, derives the facing basis and acos angle from the node position (model+0x324..0x33C) and hands the aim to Math_Vec3_LookAtRotationMatrix.
evidence: Confirmed by the s_Skull_Run string literal it stores and by the identical body at 0x005929EC (battle twin); the pose update itself is the whole function.

name: maybe_Fx_UpdateParticleListI
signature: int maybe_Fx_UpdateParticleListI(int self, int particle, int keyframe, int flags)
summary: Per-emitter sprite-quad batch: walks the particle's child chain, emits sprite quads through Fx_EmitParticleSprite, applies the particle rotation and advances the shared vertex-stream pointer.
evidence: Called by Fx_UpdateParticleListQ for emitter kind 5; the sprite-quad callees are named but the batch sizes/offsets are decompiler inferences, so the 'ListI' variant stays unproven.

name: maybe_Fx_UpdateEmitterTransform
summary: Emitter frame update that also rebuilds the emitter transform: runs the randomize-spawn step, builds the transform matrices, updates the target and destroys the emitter when its timeline expires.
evidence: Only caller is Fx_UpdateParticleTrail, and the body is near-identical to 0x0052C26C, so which of the pair is the frame update and which the transform update is unsettled.

name: maybe_Battle_UiFlow_CalcEffectWeight
signature: unsigned long long maybe_Battle_UiFlow_CalcEffectWeight(MenuState* menuState, int resistanceClassIndex, unsigned actorId, unsigned memberValue)
summary: Sums a per-member value over the battle party list for a resistance/class index 0..6, weighting it with the 1/8/16/32/64/128/256 table and dividing by the member count, to produce one effect-list row weight.
evidence: Corrected the subsystem: the only caller is Battle_UiFlow_BuildEffectList and the body walks battle work +0x4260, so 'Menu_CalcColumnFlags' named neither the caller nor the result; the weight table is what it builds.

name: maybe_Ui_ChildTransform_UpdateRotatedRow
summary: Lays out the up-to-0x20 children at self+0xB64 as a rotating row, deriving each child's position and rotation from the parent transform and the ring angle with std_FastSinCos.
evidence: No callers (virtual update); callees Ui_DataPanel_ResetRowsByIndexList and Gfx_SpritePane_GetPrimaryMaterial point at a UI data panel, but the child-transform class is inferred.

name: maybe_Gfx_SpriteActor_CreateFromDescriptor
summary: Allocates a 0x2A0-byte object, fills a 0x23-word descriptor from constants and creates the sprite actor and its mesh through Gfx_SpriteActor_CreateFromTable / Gfx_CreateSpriteMesh.
evidence: Corrected the object: the callees are sprite-actor creation and destruction (Gfx_SpriteActor_CreateFromTable, Gfx_CreateSpriteMesh, Gfx_SpriteActor_Dtor) and the allocation is a sprite actor, not an animation instance; no caller identifies the table that uses it.

name: maybe_Fx_EmitParticlesRandomRadius
summary: Emission variant that draws one random radius factor, multiplies it by the emitter radius and a square root, and hands each spawned particle to the shared quad builder.
evidence: No caller; Fx_BuildParticleRenderQuad/Fx_InitSpawnedParticle are named, but the radial distribution is inferred from the arithmetic only.

name: maybe_Fx_EmitParticlesRandomOriented
summary: Emission variant that draws three random angles and multiplies them into a rotation matrix so each spawned particle gets its own orientation before the quad is built.
evidence: No caller; the three angle draws plus the 0x0012551C matrix multiply support the oriented reading, but the variant is not corroborated.

name: maybe_Fx_EmitParticlesRing
summary: Ring/disc emission: takes a random radius factor, scales it by (1 - distance/radius) and a square root, orients the offset with the 16-byte RNG table at 0x005209A8 and writes the quad.
evidence: The shared quad builder is named, but 'ring' comes only from the radial factor; its callers (Fx_DestroyEmitter, Fx_Group_DestroyEmitters) do not look like emission call sites at all.

name: maybe_Fx_EmitParticlesSphere
summary: Spherical-shell emission: computes the radius as sqrt((1-r) + r^2*(1-r)) so particles land on the emitter's sphere surface, then builds the quad.
evidence: Fx_BuildParticleRenderQuad is named and the shell formula is visible, but no caller or constant confirms the sphere emitter type.

name: maybe_Fx_EmitParticlesOriented
summary: Fully oriented emission: builds a 4x4 basis from the three stored angles, optionally rotates the particle direction and writes the quad for every spawned particle.
evidence: Callers are the particle integrators (Fx_UpdateParticleE, 0x005237C4, 0x00524390, 0x00526F38); the matrix build is clear but the 'oriented' emitter type is inferred.

name: maybe_Fx_EmitParticlesCone
summary: Cone-shaped emission: advances the emitter lifetime accumulator, computes the radial falloff and emits each particle through the shared quad builder.
evidence: No caller; the falloff arithmetic and the shared builder fit a cone, but nothing names the emitter type.

name: maybe_Fx_EmitParticlesArc
summary: Arc-shaped emission: steps the angle by 1/(count-1) and emits particles along the rotating axis through the shared quad builder.
evidence: No caller; the even-angle stepping is visible but is not corroborated by any named caller or constant.

name: maybe_Fx_EmitParticlesRandomB
summary: Random-distribution emission variant using one RNG draw, a square root and the shared quad builder; it differs from its siblings only in inherited emitter fields.
evidence: Only the shared builder is confident; its one caller (Os_ReadChunkedTable) is unrelated on its face and no constant distinguishes the variant.

name: maybe_Fx_EmitParticlesRandomOrientedB
summary: Random-orientation emission variant: one RNG draw, a matrix multiply and two square roots, writing the orientation fields before the quad build.
evidence: Same body family as 0x005227C8 / 0x005232C8 and no caller or constant separates the three copies.

name: maybe_Fx_EmitParticlesRandomOrientedC
summary: Third random-orientation emission copy, differing from 0x00522BA8 only in which particle fields it inherits from the emitter.
evidence: No external evidence distinguishes this copy from 0x00522BA8; only the shared builder and init callees are named.

name: maybe_Fx_EmitParticlesRadialC
summary: Radial emission variant driven by the emitter lifetime accumulator: computes a random radius and writes the particle quad.
evidence: The shared builder is named; the radial shape and the unexplained u32 return are not corroborated by any caller.

name: maybe_Fx_EmitParticlesRadialD
summary: Radial emission variant with one square root per particle and a different RNG table, which suggests a flat-disc distribution.
evidence: Only the shared builder is named; the flat-disc reading comes from the arithmetic alone.

name: maybe_Fx_UpdateParticleListJ
signature: float maybe_Fx_UpdateParticleListJ(int self, float dt, float* particle, float* extra)
summary: Per-emitter update variant: integrates the particle, resolves the parent transform, emits sprite quads and links the particle into the active/free lists.
evidence: Called by Fx_UpdateParticleListQ for emitter kind 6; the heavy FP control flow and the unnamed sprite variant leave the role described rather than proven.

name: maybe_Field2D_Sprite_BuildTransformMatrix
summary: Builds a 2D sprite world matrix: either billboarded toward the camera through Camera_SetupLookAtBasis/Camera_SetupPerspective, or from the sprite's own rotation, plus scale and translation.
evidence: No callers; the billboard-vs-own-rotation branch is clear but the sprite class is inferred.

name: maybe_Field2D_Sprite_BuildTransformMatrixB
summary: Byte-identical twin of 0x005B0430: same billboard/own-rotation sprite matrix build with scale and translation.
evidence: Same body and callee set as 0x005B0430 and no caller identifies which sprite class selects this copy.

name: maybe_Gfx_UpdateScreenEntries
summary: Per-frame update of the screen view entries: walks the two 0xABC-byte screen blocks, updates each entry's transform and copies the resulting basis vectors before updating the draw list.
evidence: The only caller is Ui_SceneFlow_Update, which pins the per-frame timing but not a Gfx owner; the two-block layout is read from offsets, so the screen-entry reading stays inferred.

name: Ui_Overlay_ComputeDistanceScale
signature: void Ui_Overlay_ComputeDistanceScale(float* out, float* pos, float* scale)
summary: Builds a billboard/overlay scale from the distance between a world point and the reference object at work+0x74, clamps it to the configured limits and optionally applies the actor field factor.
evidence: Confirmed by both named callers, Ui_Overlay_UpdateTransform and Ui_Window_ProjectWorldSlot, which add the returned offset to the overlay position; the only callee is Os_GetGameWork, so the maths is self-contained.

name: maybe_Monster_Model_ApplyVariant
signature: u32 maybe_Monster_Model_ApplyVariant(MonsterModel* model, MonsterModelContext* context, u32 arg3, u32 arg4)
summary: Applies one optional monster-model variant: for context states 0x151/0x21B it creates the variant object, toggles the animation layers with the variant scale and then runs Anim_UpdateChannels / Model_UpdateMotionState.

name: maybe_Event_ActorModels_SetModelAnim
signature: void maybe_Event_ActorModels_SetModelAnim(EventActorModels* actorModels, u32 archive, EventModel* model, u32 animId)
summary: Switches an event actor's model animation: builds the '%s.ani' resource name, loads it from the archive, resolves the model entry and applies it, with a special path for expression 0x36.
evidence: Event_ActorModels_FindModelByHandle and Model_IsInstance are named callees, but the only caller is the corrupted 0x0060488C and the body has in_ZR/in_r12 damage; a simplified variant exists at 0x004B979C.

name: maybe_Fx_EmitParticlesFromGlobalVelocity
summary: Particle spawn loop that takes each particle's velocity from the global constant vector instead of the emitter's random table, clamps the spawn count and hands each particle to the shared quad builder.
evidence: No caller; the global-vector initialisation and the shared Fx_BuildParticleRenderQuad / Fx_InitSpawnedParticle callees support the reading, but the emitter type that selects it is inferred.

name: maybe_Fx_EmitParticlesRadialSpread
summary: Emitter spawn routine that builds particle quads through Fx_BuildParticleRenderQuad / Fx_InitSpawnedParticle; the radial-spread reading rests only on the square roots and the axis constants.
evidence: No callers; the body matches the sibling emission variants but the shape is inferred.

name: maybe_Fx_EmitParticlesBox
summary: Emitter spawn routine that splits the spawn count between two axes with the LCG and offsets particles along the chosen axis.
evidence: Callers are the unnamed 0x00524390 / 0x00526F38; the two-axis split is the only evidence for the box shape.

name: maybe_Gfx_CharModel_UpdateProjMatrices
summary: When the per-slot dirty flag is set, computes the inverse of the slot's 4x4 transform, writes it into the projection-texture matrix slots and rebuilds the render state.
evidence: Only caller is Gfx_Model_DrawOverlayPasses; the matrix work is named (Fx_DistributionTable_WriteEntry, Math_TransformOffsetPoint, Gfx_InitStaticDescriptors) but which resource the slots represent is unproven.

name: maybe_Node_InitAttachmentFromParent
signature: void maybe_Node_InitAttachmentFromParent(NodeAttachment* node, u32 arg2, u32 arg3, u32 arg4)
summary: Initialises an attachment node: sets the defaults, copies the parent's twelve transform words into f_40..f_64 and resolves the 'N_ALL' anchor id into f_94.
evidence: No callers; the parent-transform copy and Ui_Overlay_GetAnchorIdByName("N_ALL") are clear, and the absence of any allocation rules out a constructor, but the node type stays inferred.

name: maybe_Field_Gimmick_ApplyPartTint
summary: Builds a model descriptor from a part name and applies the formation tint through Field_ActorGroup_ApplyFormation.
evidence: Callers are two unnamed gimmick helpers; Field_ActorGroup_ApplyFormation and Field_Gimmick_InitComponentC fit, but the tint property mapping is inferred.

name: Gfx_ModelPart_InitMeshOnly
summary: Minimal model-part initialiser: copies the position params, registers a fixed two-entry fCol colour block at scale 1.0 and creates the mesh from params[3] - no sprite child and no rotation step.
evidence: Confirmed as a description of the body: it is the strict subset of the fuller part initialiser (only Gfx_AddFColAnimator + Gfx_CreateMeshObjectByParams) called by the spawn block 0x0035C758; only the caller is still unnamed.

name: maybe_Fx_UpdateEmitterFrame
summary: Advances an emitter timeline from the owner clock at +0x53C, destroys the emitter when the timeline expires and updates the target/curve/transform sub-emitters.
evidence: No callers and near-identical to 0x0052F10C, so the frame-vs-transform split between the two copies remains an interpretation.

name: maybe_Field_ComputeLocalMoveDirection
signature: void maybe_Field_ComputeLocalMoveDirection(FieldActorMoveTask* self, float* dir, float* outLen)
summary: Normalises the combined field move vector, returns its length through outLen and rotates it into the actor's facing frame, using the live camera/actor matrix at work+0x74 or the saved copy when hasOwnRotation is set.
evidence: Corrected the action: nothing here clamps anything - it normalises Field_GetCombinedMoveVector and rotates it by the actor frame; the owning class is still inferred since there are no callers.

name: maybe_Actor_UpdateSpinTransform
summary: Per-frame spin motion: integrates the angular speed, builds the rotation from sin/cos and composes it into the attached node matrix.
evidence: No callers; the sin/cos plus matrix composition is clear, but the spin source (which field drives it) is inferred.

name: maybe_Actor_Action_MoveWithEffect
summary: Movement step of an action: integrates velocity into the owner position while the countdown runs, snaps to the destination on the last step and starts the arrival effect.
evidence: No named caller identifies the action, so the countdown/velocity reading stays a description of the body.

name: maybe_Ui_Billboard_UpdateFromActor
summary: Places a billboard sprite from its owning actor: releases the stale attach slot, copies the actor position and scale into the sprite transform and applies the fade/rotation constants.

name: maybe_Ui_Window_UpdateWorldTransform
summary: Recomputes the window render transform: copies the stored translation and default basis when f_91 is set, then selects either the stored offset or the live scene-node position based on f_93.
evidence: No callers; the transform copy is clear but the window class is unconfirmed.

name: maybe_Field_EffectNode_SetupFromDesc
signature: void maybe_Field_EffectNode_SetupFromDesc(u32* effectNode, const u32* spawnDescriptor)
summary: Sets up a field effect node from its spawn descriptor: stores the descriptor fields, adds the sprite child and applies the placement using the game work and the named-row checks.
evidence: Only caller is the unnamed spawn block 0x003512C8 (maybe_Field_SceneSpawnBlock_EffectNodeFromDesc) and the signature is damaged, so the node class is inferred from that caller.

name: maybe_Actor_Action_IvyNut_Update
summary: Per-frame IvyNut action update: eases the actor toward the action target with std_Powf and selects the attract animation.

name: maybe_Map_Object_UpdatePlacementScale
signature: void maybe_Map_Object_UpdatePlacementScale(MapObject* mapObject, int arg2, int arg3, int arg4)
summary: Resolves the placement record through the map work, reads the 3D scale factors, applies them to the actor transform and places the object with Map_PlaceObject(owner, 0).
evidence: Vtable slot 0x00779E38 and the named Map_PlaceObject callee fit, but no named caller confirms the placement path.

name: maybe_Data_SoundStreamResetPadding
summary: Not a function: 0x00541F10 is the 12-byte literal data slot immediately before the ARM entry Sound_StreamBuffer_Reset at 0x00541F1C (a 1.0f and two zero words). The readable C shown is Reset's body.
evidence: Corrected the object: disassembly decodes 0x00541F10 as literal 0x3F800000/zeros and 0x00541F1C as the real ARM entry already named Sound_StreamBuffer_Reset, so this address must not be named or called as a routine.

name: maybe_Gfx_Scene_WalkNodesAndIntersectB

summary: Scene-graph walk that tests ray/mesh intersections for query variant B: recursive node descent with Math_MatrixInverse, bounds and Y-quaternion helpers.

evidence: Only named caller is Gfx_Scene_TestSpriteHitC; the two unreachable-block removals mean the recursion depth and result packing are inferred.

name: maybe_Field_Char_UpdateModelOffset
summary: Blends a character's model position offset toward a target using a clamped progress factor and std_Powf, then selects an attract animation on the target actor.
evidence: No callers; the offset blend is clear but the owning subsystem is only the parameter type.

name: maybe_Snd_ReleaseFinishedStreamTransfers
summary: Reaps completed stream transfers: walks the live-slot bitmask of the four transfer queues, releases finished blocks under the monitor, returns the slots to the free list and records completion.
evidence: Corrected the owner: the single caller is Snd_StreamManager_Update and it takes the monitor around the free-list hand-back, so this is the sound stream-transfer queue, not a Gfx upload queue; the queue internals are still unnamed helpers.

name: maybe_Ui_LoadingScreen_Update
summary: Timed transition step: accumulates elapsed time against a threshold, creates a 0x1C state object, blocks input through the manager vtable and completes the load.
evidence: No callers; Ui_GetCore, Anim_Sequence_CtorBase and Sound_SetVoiceGainByHandle fit a transition, but nothing proves it is a loading screen rather than another timed transition.

name: maybe_Gfx_BuildOrthonormalTransform
signature: void maybe_Gfx_BuildOrthonormalTransform(void* scratch, CameraTransformOut* out, u32* arg3, u32 token)
summary: Builds an orthonormal transform from the two basis/position pairs at work+0x74, normalises them and writes the position plus the 3x3 rotation.
evidence: No caller, no vtable entry and the only callee is Os_GetGameWork; the maths is the same as 0x004A06E0, so the subsystem attribution is unproven.

name: Fx_UpdateParticleB
summary: Per-particle update for emitter type B: integrates the position, dispatches the three per-emitter update tables and applies the scale/rotation/lifetime curves.
evidence: Confirmed by the two named list updaters that call it once per particle (Fx_UpdateParticleListL, Fx_UpdateParticleListM) and by the shared Fx particle pipeline; the letter is an ordinal.

name: Fx_UpdateParticleC
summary: Per-particle update for emitter type C: re-caches the emitter transform, integrates the velocity, applies the four fade factors and writes the world position into the render node.
evidence: Confirmed by the named callers Fx_UpdateParticleListN / Fx_UpdateParticleListO (one call per particle) and by the shared transform-cache callee.

name: Fx_UpdateParticleF
summary: Per-particle integration for emitter type F: transforms the velocity through the emitter basis, updates the sprite/scale accumulators, recomputes the normals and applies the colour/state step.
evidence: Confirmed by its named caller Fx_UpdateParticleListL (one call per particle in the else branch) and by the shared particle pair interpolation; only the letter is arbitrary.

name: maybe_Ui_Talk_CheckLineLength
summary: Looks up a dialogue/layout record by id, scales its signed length byte by the talk context factor and compares the result against the layout limit at +0xA8.
evidence: Only caller is Ui_ListWindow_SelectEntry and the record lookup (0x0063DA3C family) is shared with dialogue layout code, but what the scaled byte measures is unproven.

name: Field_ActorAction_CheckFacingTarget
signature: u64 Field_ActorAction_CheckFacingTarget(void* self, u32 mode, void* target)
summary: Action vtable slot: computes the dot product between the actor orientation and the direction to the target, then ORs the in-front (1) or behind (4) bit into the actor motion flags at +0x290.
evidence: Confirmed by its presence in five action vtables and by the pure dot-product/flag write; there is no direct bl caller because it is only invoked through the vtable, which also explains the empty caller list.

name: maybe_Gfx_BuildSegmentBasis
summary: Derives a marker segment from the two points at work+0x74: normalises the direction, writes start + direction*8 and builds the orthonormal basis.
evidence: No caller or vtable entry; the segment construction is clear but the attribution is unproven (same maths family as 0x003F3E90).

name: maybe_Os_LookupParamEntry
summary: Reads a 0x40-byte parameter header, searches its four 0x10-byte entries for type byte 0 and unpacks two 12-bit fields plus the payload, falling back to a block scan and the fixed 0x800/0x800/1.0 defaults.
evidence: No readable caller (only the damaged 0x0011E0DC pair); the calibration-like defaults do not identify which table this reads.

name: maybe_Os_ComputeDeadline
signature: void maybe_Os_ComputeDeadline(float* now, u32* base, u32* out, u32 request)
summary: Converts the current system tick (svc 0x28 GetSystemTick) and a packed timeout field into a 64-bit deadline using the 1e6 scaling constants and a shift of 0x12.
evidence: Caller list is empty in the current graph (the old Save_AsyncReadWorker link is gone); the svc 0x28 plus 64-bit scaling is clear but the time unit is inferred.

name: maybe_Math_EulerAnglesToVector
signature: void maybe_Math_EulerAnglesToVector(float* out, float angleX, float angleY, float angleZ)
summary: Builds a rotation from three axis angles with sin/cos/sqrt blocks and writes the resulting first basis vector to out.
evidence: The maths family is confirmed by Math_QuatMultiply neighbours, but the angles arrive in in_s0..in_s2 and the only caller (0x00623DF0) is unnamed, so the argument order stays a guess.

name: maybe_Gfx_PlaceAlongViewDirection
summary: Places the object self+0x24 units along the horizontal direction from the camera toward the player, storing the result in self+0x14/0x18/0x1C and setting self+0x28 = 1.
evidence: No caller; the direction/normalise/scale/store sequence is clean, but it is a descriptive name for a layout-only routine (no view-matrix update).

name: maybe_Field_NpcPlayNutAndFaceTarget
summary: Field-NPC gesture: plays the 'Nut' motion unless mode is 0xC, switches the model pose, turns the NPC toward the linked actor and sets the wrong-facing byte.
evidence: The 'Nut' literal at 0x0074754E is shared with the named 0x0074754E-family motion setter, but no caller confirms the pose/linked-actor reading.

name: maybe_Ui_Window_ApplyActorProjection
signature: void maybe_Ui_Window_ApplyActorProjection(void* window, u32 arg2, u32 arg3, void* outMatrix, u32 mode)
summary: Window virtual (vtable 0x00765508 slot 7): builds a projection matrix for the attached 3D actor, selects one of two stored frustum constants for mode 2/3, fills the matrix and applies it to the node.
evidence: No named caller (vtable-only) and the two matrix helpers used to fill it are unnamed, so the window/actor projection reading is inferred from the slot neighbourhood.

name: maybe_Actor_Action_GrabNut_Update
summary: Per-frame GrabNut action update: blends the owner model position toward its target with the std_Powf easing curve.
evidence: No callers; it repeats the position-offset easing of 0x004CE218 (IvyNut) and only std_Powf is named, so the GrabNut attribution is inherited from the neighbouring action data.

name: maybe_Fx_RenderBatch_Init
summary: Constructor of a render-batch object: zeroes the 0x1D8-byte header, builds three intrusive lists from the same list template and sets the default depth/near-far values 240.0/400.0.
evidence: No caller; the one-shot constructor shape is clear (0x1D8 bytes zeroed, three list heads, defaults) but the render-batch owner is inferred.

name: maybe_Gfx_InitTextureSlotUV
signature: void maybe_Gfx_InitTextureSlotUV(int self, int slot, int enabled)
summary: Per-slot texture setup: stores the enable flag, reads the two dimensions out of the tagged 0x82 descriptor record through Gfx_Resource_FindSizeRecord when enabled, converts them to floats and resets the slot UV rectangle to (0,0)-(1,1).
evidence: No callers and no vtable reference; the descriptor consumption is the only evidence, and the same tagged records are used by the named glyph/overlay builders.

name: maybe_Anim_BuildSampleBuffer
signature: void maybe_Anim_BuildSampleBuffer(AnimTrackTable* src, void* values, void* dest)
summary: Builds the multi-track animation sampling working buffer: calculates the per-track strides and allocates the sampling segments.
evidence: Reachable only through the animation track dispatch tables; the track element format and the buffer layout remain unverified.

name: Gfx_Actor_FinishMotion
summary: Finishes the actor's current motion: releases the handle-table entry, applies the final transform, copies the stored rotation, toggles the scene flag, re-finalises the actor, clears the motion handle and returns 1 when a motion was active.
evidence: Confirmed by the two named callers ActorAimTarget / ActorAimTargetDirect and by the named Gfx_HandleTable_Release plus the Gfx_EffectPart_Set* callees on the same object.

name: Ui_Widget_UpdateFadeTween
summary: Tween step for a UI widget's embedded fade: runs a small 0..4 state machine, interpolates the element alpha toward the target and accumulates the phase; states 4/reset restore the initial values.
evidence: Corrected the scope: it is not text-specific - its 13 callers include Ui_Widget_StartTween, Battle_UnitModel_StartTween, Event_ActorModels_Update, Ui_Balloon_UpdateForMember and BattleScene_SetUnitFadeFull, and its sibling vtable slots hold the widget's start/stop tween entries, so it is the shared widget fade tween update.

name: Field_ActorAction_TurnActionCtor
summary: Tiny action constructor: runs Action_CtorBase, installs the g_fieldActorTurnActionVtable vtable and stores 0.6f / 1.0f / 0.
evidence: Corrected the identity: the ctor stores the named vtable g_fieldActorTurnActionVtable, so this is the turn-action subclass (B was a placeholder), even though its only caller is Model_AttachAccessoriesAndWeapons.

name: maybe_Battle_UnitModel_HidePartnerPart
signature: void maybe_Battle_UnitModel_HidePartnerPart(UnitModel* self, int arg2, int arg3)
summary: Resets the unit-model display values (scale 1.0, timer 10, flag 1) and, for the unit with model id 0x350, performs two disable-style virtual calls on its vtable +0x50 and on the attached model's +0x4C.

name: maybe_Ui_Gauge_StartValueAnimation

summary: Initialises a gauge fill animation: clamps the input ratio, converts it to a 2400-unit counter, stores the start/end counters and callback ids, finds the 'gauge_line' pane and starts the widget animation.

name: maybe_Math_EaseCurve_Vec2BackOut

name: maybe_Gfx_NewRenderQueue

name: Os_Timer_ConvertTicks
signature: void Os_Timer_ConvertTicks(s64* outMs, int stem, s64 ticksA, int stemB, u32 perSecond, int scale)

evidence: Confirmed by the 1000-inverse magic plus the final multiply by 1000 and by three callers from unrelated subsystems (Svc_Ir_SetupChannel, Fs_ReadRecordBlock, 0x00122484) that all need a shared time conversion.

name: maybe_Trail_UpdateDirection
summary: Lazily builds the shared 0x1C-stride pool on first use, then aims self's +0x9C vector from the pool object's +0xB0 base along the normalised +0x224..0x22C direction scaled by +0x230 and sets the dirty byte +0x118.
evidence: No callers; the pool allocation is only the lazy prefix of a per-frame direction update and the trailing call is 0x005F6558, so the trail attribution comes from that twin.

name: maybe_Ui_MessagePart_ApplyFadeParams
signature: void maybe_Ui_MessagePart_ApplyFadeParams(int self, u32 arg2, u32 arg3, u32 part)
summary: Builds a fade parameter block from float literals scaled by an incoming float, hands it to the unnamed helper 0x00125558 and starts the layout's fade animation through virtual +0x30.
evidence: No callers, the callee is unnamed and the float argument arrives in in_s0, so both the message-part owner and the fade reading stay inferred.

name: maybe_Sound_CalcDspAdpcmStep
summary: Computes two 16-bit sound-voice coefficients (with a square-root term) from a scale/step pair, stores them at +8/+10 and copies them into the DSP register block with dirty flag 8.
evidence: Four named sound callers (Sound_Voice_ApplyPendingParams, Sound_Voice_UpdatePlayState, Snd_InitChannels, Gfx_MovieTrack_Start) pin the sound-voice math, but the exact 'ADPCM step' meaning is still inferred.

name: Fx_UpdateEmitterTarget
signature: void Fx_UpdateEmitterTarget(FxEmitter* self, int arg2, int target)
summary: Interpolates the emitter position toward its target in fixed steps and invokes the per-step callback from the table at 0x007AEB6C for the intermediate positions.
evidence: Confirmed by both named emitter update variants (0x0052C26C, 0x0052F10C) calling it as their shared target interpolation; only the callback table entries remain unnamed.

name: maybe_Math_ClampUnitRatio
signature: float* maybe_Math_ClampUnitRatio(float* out, int record, int flags, int count)
summary: Damaged Thumb routine (74 bytes) that appears to clamp a ratio to [0,1] and walk a record list; the body cannot be re-derived (coprocessor_function, unaff_r7).
evidence: Only caller is the unnamed 0x00627404 and the decompilation is unusable, so no contract can be verified.

name: maybe_Sound_InitWaveBlock
summary: Clears the caller's offset word, zero-fills the 0x50-byte block at self+0x1AB4 and stores float 1.0 as its first word (default gain).
evidence: No callers; which sound sub-object lives at +0x1AB4 is a guess, so the 'wave block' wording stays unproven.

name: maybe_Ui_Widget_BeginSubTweenIn
summary: Initialises the widget's tween block with duration 10, progress 0 and the active byte set, after querying the controller at +0x14.
evidence: The whole sibling family (StartSubTween/StopSubTween/BeginSubTweenOut) is still maybe_, and the constant 10 is the only hard fact here.

name: maybe_Monster_Model_InitSubObject
summary: Initialises the model's embedded sub-object: sets slot byte +0x1DC to 0xFF, re-creates the animation handle through 0x0047E1FC on +0x144, restores the default scale 1.0f and points the sub-object vtable at self+0x2D4.
evidence: Vtable slot only (no named siblings) and the one named callee is Battle_Ui_UnitModel_ApplyZOffset, so the 'Monster_Model' owner is inferred.

name: maybe_Fx_CopyEmitterBaseTransformScaled
summary: Copies the emitter base transform like 0x00524C68 but first scales the particle scale by f_300 + (1-f_300)*(1-dt), so a fading particle inherits a shrunken base transform.
evidence: The fade re-scaling lerp with in_s0 is clear and the copy matches its twin 0x00524C68, but the field meaning is inferred and there are no callers.

name: maybe_Gfx_EffectPart_ApplyRowFadeConfig
signature: void maybe_Gfx_EffectPart_ApplyRowFadeConfig(unsigned arg1, unsigned rowKey, int rowIndex)
summary: Looks up an 8-byte-stride table entry by row index, checks its stored key against rowKey>>6, starts the row animation and applies fade/duration values (1.0f, 0.209f) to the effect part obtained from 0x005F5818.
evidence: Corrected the object: the callees are Anim_ActionSeq_StepFrame and Gfx_EffectPart_ResetToDefault and the writes go to an effect part, so 'Ui_ScrollList' was wrong; the row table owner is still unnamed.

name: maybe_SequenceBase_StepSlotCursor
summary: Shared sequence base-class step: counts the 16 active slot pointers at self+0x1C and, in state 0x144B, walks the slot cursor at self+0x490, waiting on each slot's vt[+0x14] / vt[+0x10] and spawning an event balloon per slot; returns 1 and resets the cursor once every slot is done.
evidence: Corrected the scope: 26 callers span battle UI, battle action sequences and Ui_TalkWindow_RunMessageState, and the loop is over 16 slot pointers with per-slot vtable polling, so 'FieldParty_AdvanceMemberCursor' was far too narrow; the base class itself is still unnamed.

name: maybe_Battle_ActorAction_Sequence
signature: u32* maybe_Battle_ActorAction_Sequence(void* self, void* action, void* ctx, void* out)
summary: Long multi-stage battle actor action (3.3 KB): plays the record's SE cues, moves the actor toward its target, spawns popups and effects per record id and returns a pointer into the action data.
evidence: Callers are Battle_ActorAction_UpdateComposite and 0x004359B8, and the callees are named (Battle_MessageQueue_PushEntry, Ui_PopupEntry_SpawnCountBalloon, Sound_PlaySeById, Battle_IsActionQueueIdle), but the body has halt_baddata and undecoded stages, so the name stays generic.

name: Field_Gimmick_LayoutConfiguredParts
summary: Positions the configured parts of a gimmick: applies the configured offset around the actor, sets the tint through the label object and plays the SE for each part.
evidence: Confirmed by its named caller Field_Gimmick_ApplyConfigBlock (the configuration source) plus the part loop with Field_SceneObject_ShowAndSelectEntry / Sound_PlaySeById.

name: maybe_Ui_Entry_FillStyleParam
signature: unsigned char* maybe_Ui_Entry_FillStyleParam(void* style, int entryIndex, int alternate, unsigned int amount)
summary: Fills a small style descriptor (kind 4, value 0xE) from weighted random rolls against the per-entry float at +0x188.
evidence: Only caller is the unnamed 0x00378E8C and the body mixes RNG with a style byte write; nothing pins the descriptor semantics.

name: maybe_Field2D_Sprite_UpdateAnimation
summary: Four-state 2D sprite movement step: advances the timer, interpolates the position in state 0, builds the curve record in state 1, follows it in state 2 and finishes in state 3.
evidence: No callers; Gfx_Actor_SetPositionXY, Math_Curve_EvaluatePoint and Gfx_Trail_TryConnectCell fit a sprite/curve step, but the class and state meanings are inferred.

name: maybe_Ui_SceneFlow_OpenSceneField
summary: Scene handler for the field variant: at state 9 it resets the render mode, configures the camera from the scene descriptor, binds the field scene object ids and pushes the message/fade descriptor.
evidence: No callers, and the 'field variant' rests on the absence of a slot id; the body is surrounded by named Ui_SceneFlow_* / Field_Level_LoadResources / Cutscene_Init helpers, so the subsystem is right but the entry point is unproven.

name: maybe_Ui_SceneFlow_AdvanceCutscene
summary: Scene-flow step for states 9/10/11: calls Ui_SceneFlow_AdvanceState, then for state 9 starts the cutscene (Cutscene_Init / Event_OnCutSceneCommand / Cutscene_ApplyLayerFlags); other states load the world-map models and advance the counter.
evidence: The decompilation is truncated by halt_baddata, so only the state-9 branch is verified; the name describes that branch.

name: maybe_SceneFlow_ApplyStateResource
signature: void maybe_SceneFlow_ApplyStateResource(u32 handle, const char* record)
summary: Applies a scene-state record to a packed UI resource: selects an FS transfer priority 0..4 from the record bytes, releases the handle's 20 entries and picks UI palette entry 7 or 4 by comparing the old and new state bytes.
evidence: Corrected the owner: all five callers are scene-flow transitions (Ui_SceneFlow_TeardownAll, SceneFlow_TryCommitTransition, Ui_SceneFlow_AdvanceState, Ui_SceneFlow_Release2dCommonPack), and the body does transfer-priority plus palette selection, so 'Ui_Window_SetColorByState' covered only half of it.

name: maybe_Script_SetBookCommandParams
summary: Publishes four parameters to the running .cnut script while the script object is active (guarded by f_94), using the four pooled names g_002555E4..g_002555F0.
evidence: The shape matches the named parameter setter at 0x00253EA0 and both callers use it after loading an event script, but the 'book' attribution comes only from the four pooled strings.

name: maybe_Gfx_Overlay_DrawFourQuads
signature: void maybe_Gfx_Overlay_DrawFourQuads(OverlayCtx* overlayCtx, u32 arg2, u32 arg3)
summary: Overlay quad submit path called from Gfx_Overlay_BeginDraw; the middle of the body is lost (in_s0/in_d8, halt_baddata), so neither the quad count nor the layer mapping is proven.
evidence: Caller Gfx_Overlay_BeginDraw and the render-context/command-buffer callees support an overlay draw path, but the body is damaged and 'FourQuads' is unverifiable.
